# coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-core-stepcounter

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

Two agents, one feature each, with messaging and a shared git remote, on the `core` subset (10 pairs chosen to represent the full benchmark, including three pairs where both features change the same function). Setup: `gemini-3.8-flash` at `high` thinking, 100 steps, compaction at 28K, and the per-turn step counter. Compared with `solo` on the same pairs (5/10), it looks for coordination failures that `flash_10` rarely shows.

## Observations

- 4/10, against 5/10 for `solo` on the same pairs. The runs disagree on three pairs: `solo` passed `llama_index_task/17244` and `pallets_jinja_task/1559` where `coop` passed only one feature, and `coop` passed `pallets_jinja_task/1621` where `solo` pushed nothing.
- Both merge conflicts in the run came from pairs where the two features change the same function: `dspy_task/8563` and `react_hook_form_task/153`. The third such pair, `go_chi_task/27`, merged cleanly but only feature B passed, as in `solo`. These are the coordination failures `core` was chosen to surface: with `gemini-3.8-flash`, none of the `flash_10` runs had more than one conflict.
- 19 of 20 agents pushed work, and 7 of 20 used all 100 steps (all 10 did in `solo`). Agents sent 23 messages per pair on average, more than on `flash_10` (17).
- 23 calls were retried because of the API rate limit.
